record.title: The v-number conjecture for crown graphs
record.statement:
Let $G=C_{n,n}$ with $n \ge 4$. The graph $G$ is the crown graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph on two parts of size $n$ by deleting a perfect matching, and $J_G$ denotes its binomial edge ideal. For $T \in \mathcal{C}(G)$, let $P_T(G)$ be the corresponding prime ideal and let $\operatorname{v}_{P_T(G)}(J_G)$ denote the local v-number of $J_G$ at $P_T(G)$. **The v-number conjecture for crown graphs.** For every $T \in \mathcal{C}(G)$, 
$$
\operatorname{v}_{P_T(G)}(J_G)=4.
$$
 This would establish the expected upper value in the bound $3\leq \operatorname{v}(J_G)\leq 4$ for crown graphs with $n\geq 4$; the case $T=\emptyset$ is already known, while the assertion for every cut-set prime remains open.
record.source_name: Arvind Kumar, Joshua Pomeroy and Le Tran, “Binomial edge ideals of crown graphs”, arXiv:2507.03889 (2025).
